CALCEXPLORER_SUBTITLE: Pick a cell from a view and follow its value through every rule, consolidation and cross-cube hop — with rule-file line numbers and an interactive HTML export.
CALCEXPLORER_DEPTHHELP: How many levels the request asks the server to build and return. Depth is a real limit and a real cost: each extra level multiplies both. Use the caret or 'trace deeper' on any node to go further from that point instead.
CALCEXPLORER_FETCHDEPTHHELP: The same setting as Trace depth on the first tab. It bounds every request from here on — the next ⊞ or 'trace deeper', and the next full trace. Changing it does not rebuild the tree already on screen; use Re-trace beside it for that. Each extra level multiplies both the time and the size.
CALCEXPLORER_RETRACEHELP: Trace this same cell again at the fetch depth beside this button. It is a full trace: at the same depth it costs what the first one cost, and every extra level multiplies it.
CALCEXPLORER_RETRACECONFIRM: This tree was built at depth {was}. Re-tracing at {now} asks the server for every level in between, and each extra level multiplies the time and the size — one cell of the demo model went 83 KB at depth 3 to 37 MB at depth 6. Re-trace at depth {now}?
CALCEXPLORER_NOVIEWS: This cube has no views you can read.
CALCEXPLORER_VIEWHELP: Click any cell in the grid to see its value and the rule that produced it. The component tree is one more click from there.
CALCEXPLORER_MDXHELP: Any MDX that returns a cellset works. Handy when the cell you want is not in a saved view.
CALCEXPLORER_WALKRUNNING: Tracing this cell — one trace runs at a time
CALCEXPLORER_WALKBUSY: A trace is already running. Tracing is one server-side walk per request, so this plugin runs one at a time — wait for it to finish.
CALCEXPLORER_OWNWALK: Your last trace is still running on the server (started {seconds}s ago). It finishes whether or not you wait — unless an administrator cancels it — and starting another now doubles what the server is doing. Trace this cell anyway?
CALCEXPLORER_OTHERWALK: Another user ({name}) is running a cell trace, started {seconds}s ago. Running two at once increases the server's memory use and slows both. Continue anyway?
CALCEXPLORER_WALKEARLIER: Your earlier trace is still running on the server
CALCEXPLORER_CANCELHELP: Stop this trace on the server — an administrator action. It frees this page and the server's worker; it does not hand back memory TM1 has already taken.
CALCEXPLORER_CANCELSENT: Cancel sent. The page will say so when the request it was waiting on comes back.
CALCEXPLORER_CANCELNOTTRACE: That thread is not a calculation trace, so this page left it alone.
CALCEXPLORER_CANCELNOTMINE: That trace belongs to another user, and stopping one needs administrator rights.
CALCEXPLORER_CANCELUNREADABLE: The server's thread list could not be read just now, so nothing was cancelled.
CALCEXPLORER_CANCELCONFIRM:
Cancel {name}'s trace of {cube}, running for {seconds}s?

Their page stops with a message saying the trace was cancelled on the server. It does not give memory back to TM1.
CALCEXPLORER_TRACECANCELLED: You cancelled this trace, so nothing came back.
CALCEXPLORER_TRACECANCELLEDOTHER: This trace was cancelled on the server, so nothing came back — an administrator can stop a running trace.
CALCEXPLORER_CANCELRESTORED: The tree that was on screen before the re-trace is back.
CALCEXPLORER_WALKCLOCK: The elapsed time is TM1's own, read from the server's thread list rather than timed in this page — a page timer keeps counting after a connection drops. While the answer is arriving it holds at the time the walk itself took. Closing or reloading this page does not stop the walk — the server finishes it either way. Cancel does stop it, and is an administrator action.
CALCEXPLORER_DRILLCONFIRM: Auto-drill re-traces at every hop, and each hop is a full server-side trace bounded to the trace depth — cheap at the default depth, and multiplied by every level you add. See Known limitations in the README. Traces this may ask the server for, at most:
CALCEXPLORER_RESOLVECONFIRM: Resolving runs one full server-side trace per boundary, each bounded to the trace depth — cheap at the default depth, and multiplied by every level you add. See Known limitations in the README. Traces this will ask the server for:
CALCEXPLORER_LEGENDCLICK: click a cell to read it
CALCEXPLORER_NOTRACE: Nothing traced yet — pick a cell on the first tab.
CALCEXPLORER_TRUNCATED: components were not shown because a node had more than the render cap. Narrow the cell or trace a child directly.
CALCEXPLORER_FRONTIERNOTE: {boundary} of the {total} nodes in this trace stop at the depth you asked for. Use Re-trace to rebuild deeper, or drill down and click ⊞ on a row to fetch the next level from there.
CALCEXPLORER_FILTERSHELP: Narrow what the tree shows: which cube, whether zero and empty cells are listed, and whether to show only rule-derived cells. The number beside it is how many are on.
CALCEXPLORER_AUTODRILLDONE: Followed the biggest contributor down. Hops:
CALCEXPLORER_IDENTICAL: identical statements in the rule file
CALCEXPLORER_NOTLOCATED: rule statement (could not be located in the cube's rule file)
CALCEXPLORER_NOMATCH: No node matches the current filters.
CALCEXPLORER_SHAREHELP: Open, save or copy this trace — the interactive HTML page, or a plain-text version.
CALCEXPLORER_COPYDONE: The trace was copied to the clipboard as text.
CALCEXPLORER_EXPORTDONE: The interactive HTML trace was saved.
CALCEXPLORER_FEEDERSHELP: Two questions about the cell on screen: what it feeds, and whether anything under it holds a rule value no feeder reaches.
CALCEXPLORER_NOFEEDERCELL: No cell chosen yet — pick one on the first tab, or right-click a cell in the cube viewer and choose Trace Feeders.
CALCEXPLORER_NOFEEDERSTATEMENTS: No feeder statements were reported for this cell.
CALCEXPLORER_NOFEDCELLS: This cell feeds nothing (or the server did not report fed cells).
CALCEXPLORER_FEDYES: Fed — TM1 reports a feeder reaching this cell. Click to read it one dimension per line.
CALCEXPLORER_FEDNO: Not fed — a statement above names this cell, but TM1 reports no feeder reaching it, so a rule value here reads as zero.
CALCEXPLORER_FEDUNKNOWN: This server did not say whether the cell is fed, which is not the same as saying it is not.
CALCEXPLORER_FEDUNFEDNOTE: {unfed} of the {total} cells these statements name are not fed: TM1 reports no feeder reaching them, so a rule value in one of them reads as zero and any consolidation over it reads low.
CALCEXPLORER_FEDUNKNOWNNOTE: Some rows carry no answer: this server did not report whether those cells are fed. That is a silence, not a verdict.
CALCEXPLORER_FEDCELLUNLABELLED: Cell not labelled by the server — it refused the expanded request, so only the fed answer came back.
CALCEXPLORER_FEDEXPANDHELP: Show this cell one dimension per line.
CALCEXPLORER_CHECKFOUND: These hold a rule value that no feeder reaches — the usual reason a consolidation reads low.
CALCEXPLORER_FEEDERSALLEMPTY: Three empty lists is a normal answer for a calculated cell: the first two are what this cell feeds, and a rule or consolidated cell usually feeds nothing. Ask about the stored cell that feeds it.
CALCEXPLORER_NOCHECKRESULT: No unfed cells found. The check looks for rule-derived cells holding a value no feeder reaches, so an empty list is the good answer — unless the area is wide enough to hit the server scan limit (CheckFeedersMaximumCells, 3,000,000 cells by default).
CALCEXPLORER_NOHISTORY: No traces yet. Every trace you run is remembered here.
CALCEXPLORER_LOADCUBESFAILED: Could not load the cube list
CALCEXPLORER_LOADVIEWSFAILED: Could not load the view list
CALCEXPLORER_BUSINESSHELP: A plainer view: only what changed at each step, one branch open at a time, biggest contributor first, technical detail behind 'why'.
CALCEXPLORER_VALUESCAP: smaller components are not listed here — drill into this row to see them.
CALCEXPLORER_NOFORMULA: No rule statement was returned for this cell — its value is stored.
CALCEXPLORER_UNMATCHED: no component reported a value for this operand
CALCEXPLORER_OPERANDJUMP: click to open this operand where it sits in the tree
CALCEXPLORER_OPERANDTRACE: click to trace this operand's own cell
CALCEXPLORER_APPROX: named from the rule, not from returned coordinates
CALCEXPLORER_RESOLVECAPPED: Stopped at the cap — run it again for the rest.
CALCEXPLORER_NORESOLVE: No labelled ancestor to re-trace from.
CALCEXPLORER_STATEMENTSELSEWHERE: more statements came back with this cell, each naming a dimension this cube does not have — they belong to components of this cell rather than to the cell, so they are not read as its formula. They are still listed under Rule below.
CALCEXPLORER_DBLEGEND: A highlighted coordinate inside a DB( ) lookup is the element TM1 reported for it, standing where the rule wrote a !dimension or a call — hover it to see what it replaced. An argument the rule spells out is left as written, and a lookup no single component could be matched to is left alone.
CALCEXPLORER_CELLREFHELP: Right-click a cell in the cube viewer, choose Cell Reference, and paste the whole table here. It is matched by dimension name, so the row order does not matter, and the hierarchy it reports is used for the trace. The dialog does not name the cube — pick that on the left first. A comma / tab separated element list in cube dimension order, or a DB('cube','element',...) formula, also work.
CALCEXPLORER_CELLREFBAD: Nothing element-like in that paste. Expected a dimension / element line per dimension, a comma-separated element list, or a DB('cube','element',...) formula.
CALCEXPLORER_DEPTHNOTE: Depth is how many levels the server builds, and the cost climbs steeply with it — for one cell of the demo model, 83 KB at depth 3, 11.8 MB at 5 and 37 MB at 6. Your own cells will differ, and a wide one differs a lot. Start low, then use the caret on a single node to go deeper from just there.
CALCEXPLORER_WHYHELP: Show how this number was worked out — the cell, its formula and the values that went into it.
CALCEXPLORER_MANYSTATEMENTS: candidate rule statements cover this cell. TM1 does not say which one fired, so the first is shown.
CALCEXPLORER_BUDGETHIT1: This trace is bigger than the plugin renders:
CALCEXPLORER_BUDGETHIT2: components were left out after the first
CALCEXPLORER_BUDGETHIT3: . Lowering the depth does help now — the request is bounded to the depth you ask for — or use the caret on one node to trace deeper from just that point.
CALCEXPLORER_DROPPEDHERE: components under here were left out at the size limit — trace deeper from this node to see them.
CALCEXPLORER_BIGEXPORT: of interactive HTML — a page that size is slow to open and too big to email. Trace a narrower cell for something shareable. Save it anyway?
CALCEXPLORER_CELLREFPLACEHOLDER:
Paste Arc's Cell Reference table here, e.g.
Dimension	Hierarchy	Element
Country and Region	Country and Region	Americas
Retailers	Retailers	ALL RETAILERS
CALCEXPLORER_CELLREFNOMATCH: none of the pasted dimension names belong to this cube.
CALCEXPLORER_CELLREFPARTIAL: dimensions were filled in from the paste — complete the rest below, then trace.
CALCEXPLORER_ROWCAP: more rows are not shown at once. Collapse a branch, or narrow the filter, to see them.
CALCEXPLORER_NOINSTANCE: No TM1 instance is selected. If the instance is still connecting, reopen this page once it is up.
CALCEXPLORER_INPUTCELL: This is a stored input cell — the value was typed in or loaded, not calculated. The trace stops here.
CALCEXPLORER_OPERANDDROPPED: An operand shown as ? was left out at the size limit, not missing from TM1 — trace deeper from this node to fetch it.
CALCEXPLORER_COORDEXPAND: Show the whole cell reference on as many lines as it needs
CALCEXPLORER_COPYCELLHELP: Copy the cell reference as text
CALCEXPLORER_COPYCELLTABLEHELP: Copy as a Dimension / Hierarchy / Element table, the shape Arc's Cell Reference uses
CALCEXPLORER_COPYCELLDONE: The cell reference was copied to the clipboard.
CALCEXPLORER_COPYCELLTABLEDONE: Copied as a dimension / hierarchy / element table.
CALCEXPLORER_COPYLINKHELP: Copy a link that reopens Calculation Explorer on this cell. Paste it to a colleague with Arc open, or keep it as a bookmark — the trace runs when the link is opened.
CALCEXPLORER_COPYLINKDONE: A link to this cell was copied to the clipboard.
CALCEXPLORER_TAKEOVERCALCHELP: Right-clicking a cell in the cube viewer and choosing Trace Calculation opens this plugin on that cell instead of Arc's built-in trace page. Untick to hand it back.
CALCEXPLORER_TAKEOVERFEEDHELP: Right-clicking a cell in the cube viewer and choosing Trace Feeders opens this plugin's Feeders tab on that cell instead of Arc's built-in feeder page. Untick to hand it back.
CALCEXPLORER_TOOKOVER: Opened here instead of Arc's built-in trace. Untick “Trace Calculation” under “Open Arc's cell menu here” on the first tab to hand it back.
CALCEXPLORER_TOOKOVERFEEDERS: Feeders checked here instead of on Arc's built-in page. Untick “Trace Feeders” under “Open Arc's cell menu here” on the first tab to hand it back.
CALCEXPLORER_FROMFEEDERSMENU: Cube viewer cell menu — Trace Feeders
CALCEXPLORER_HANDOVERFAILED: Arc handed over a cell this plugin could not read against the cube's dimensions:
CALCEXPLORER_ABOUTGUIDEHELP: Opens the illustrated guide Arc serves from this plugin's folder, so it matches the build you are running.
CALCEXPLORER_ABOUTREADS: Tracing only — this plugin never writes to your model.
CALCEXPLORER_ABOUTCONTACTHELP: E-mail Muhammad Eissa, Cubewise: questions, feedback and bug reports.
CALCEXPLORER_ABOUTCOST: A trace builds only the levels you ask for. Depth and how wide the cell is decide what it costs — the guide has the measurements.
CALCEXPLORER_BUILDTREEHELP: Ask the server for the components behind this number, bounded to the trace depth. At the default depth this is a small request; raising the depth multiplies what the server builds — see Known limitations in the plugin's README.
CALCEXPLORER_PREVIEWCOST: On the demo model, depth 3 measured 24 KB to 591 KB depending on the cell, in about two seconds. Depth multiplies it steeply — another cell went 83 KB at 3 to 11.8 MB at 5 — and a wide cell on a large model costs more than any of these.
CALCEXPLORER_PREVIEWNORULE: No rule fires on this cell — its value is stored, so this is already where the number came from. There is nothing below it to walk.
CALCEXPLORER_PREVIEWCONSOL: A consolidation: this value is the sum of its children, and the tree is the only way to see which of them it came from.
CALCEXPLORER_PREVIEWELSEWHERE: further statements came back for this cell that name a dimension this cube does not have, so they belong to its components rather than to the cell itself. Build the tree to see them where they apply.
CALCEXPLORER_BOUNDARYROW: This is as deep as the request went. Click to trace deeper from here.
CALCEXPLORER_SUMOFBOUNDED: Its components were not fetched — this node is as deep as the request went. Trace deeper from here to see them.
CALCEXPLORER_OPERANDBOUNDED: An operand shown as ? was not fetched — this node is as deep as the request went, so it is not missing from TM1. Trace deeper from here to fetch it.
CALCEXPLORER_PREVIEWBUSY: One cell at a time — this takes about a second.
CALCEXPLORER_OPENINGCELL: Opening the cell you asked for…
